red_flags.flag: Small-organisation experience: eleven staff and a 28 million shilling budget will look modest
red_flags.how: Answer it with a specific story from the file rather than a claim.

red_flags.flag: No commercial or P&L experience at all
red_flags.how: Show it through a story where the applicant made a commercial or people decision and carried others with them.

red_flags.flag: Sector and salary change that admissions readers will question the realism of
red_flags.how: Make the short-term goal specific (role, sector, place) and connect it to a story that shows the motive.

red_flags.flag: Quant 44 is the weaker half of her GMAT and her degree is non-quantitative
red_flags.how: Point to the quantitative and academic evidence elsewhere in the file in one plain paragraph; no apology and no excuse.

red_flags.flag: No international experience outside East Africa
red_flags.how: Answer it with a specific story from the file rather than a claim.

kit_properties: Every number in every draft matches the Fact Sheet or a story's own numbers.
No draft names a person whose story marks them as not to be named.
No sentence uses any of these words: passionate, empowerment, impactful, beneficiaries, journey, give back, voiceless, change-maker.

The goals essay names the short-term goal specifically: An operations or commercial role at a social enterprise selling to low-income customers in East Africa — a school group, a health provider or an off-grid energy company — where the revenue comes from the customer rather than a grant.
The leadership essay leads with "The year we stopped paying fees", or the Strategist says why another story is stronger.
The setback essay leads with "The mentor I had to remove", or the Strategist says why another story is stronger.
